parts.contentJson: {"text":"Focus on simplifying messy UI and removing any developer-style elements currently present in the system.  Design a complete end-to-end UI redesign for “LifeLink,” a hospital management system. Create a modern healthcare SaaS product for desktop and tablet. The live product includes these modules and workflows: public landing, authentication, role-aware workspace hub, admin control, application reviews, IT admissions and bed allocation, ward and care-unit setup, doctor dashboard, nurse dashboard, patient portal, donor dashboard, blood bank inventory, and blood matching operations.  Visual direction: - Modern, clean, professional healthcare UI - Soft medical palette: primary medical blue, white surfaces, teal/green secondary accents, warm amber for warning, red only for critical alerts - Rounded cards, subtle shadows, calm gradients, spacious layout, clear hierarchy - Humanist sans typography, readable dense tables, strong headers, clean iconography - Minimal but highly functional, optimized for high-pressure hospital environments  Important redesign rules: - Do not show raw JSON, backend payloads, API response panels, bearer token fields, debug consoles, or endpoint-labeled buttons in the main UI - Do not force users to type raw numeric IDs to select patients, admissions, beds, doctors, donors, or health checks; replace with searchable tables, autocomplete, pickers, selectable cards, drawers, and guided forms - Separate technical diagnostics from production UI; if an internal admin diagnostic page exists, keep it hidden as a secondary internal-only tool - Build one unified design system across all roles and modules  Create a design system first: - Color tokens, typography scale, 8px spacing system, radii, shadows, borders, grid rules - App shell with left navigation, top utility bar, page title area, breadcrumb, role badge, notification bell, and user menu - Reusable components: KPI cards, filter bars, searchable tables, row selection, status chips, tabs, segmented controls, avatars, timelines, empty states, inline alerts, toasts, modals, drawers, confirmation dialogs, pagination, skeleton loaders, form controls, date/time pickers, dropdowns, multi-select, command/search dialog  Use these status systems consistently: - Applications: Pending, Approved, Rejected - Accounts: Active, Frozen - Beds: Available, Occupied, Maintenance, Reserved - Admissions: Admitted, Discharged, Transferred, Cancelled - Appointments: Booked, Cancelled, Completed, No Show - Blood requests: Pending, Matched, Approved, Fulfilled, Rejected, Cancelled - Blood urgency: Normal, Urgent, Emergency - Blood components: Whole Blood, Plasma, Platelets, RBC - Donor notifications: Sent, Read, Acknowledged - Donor responses and matches: Suggested, Notified, Accepted, Declined, Completed  Design the full screen set:  1. Public and entry flow - Public landing page for LifeLink with healthcare SaaS messaging - Shared login page for all users - Separate registration pages for Patient, Donor, and Applicant - Role-aware workspace hub after login with shortcuts to each user’s primary destination - Clean session and profile context, never developer-style token language  2. Admin screens - Admin Control Center dashboard with KPIs, pending applicants, departments loaded, frozen accounts, and recent actions - Applicant review queue with filters, card/table view, quick approve/reject actions, review notes, and batch-friendly layout - Staff provisioning screens for doctor setup, nurse department assignment, IT worker department assignment - User account control screen with freeze/unfreeze, account status, role badges, and audit trail - Clear workflow moving from application approval to staff setup without raw-ID-only interactions  3. IT operations and bed management - IT dashboard for admissions, department scope, patient lookup, doctor lookup, available beds, and discharge flow - Ward setup and infrastructure page for care units, bed inventory, occupancy summary, and filters by department and unit type - Admissions queue with patient context, diagnosis, care level requested, active bed assignment, and urgency - Bed assignment flow with searchable available beds, side-by-side patient/admission detail, and confirmation modal - Bed occupancy summary cards and tables by department, ward, ICU, NICU, and CCU  4. Doctor experience - Doctor dashboard with profile summary, department, specialization, today’s appointments, my patients, and pending bed requests - Appointment management list with filters and cancel modal - Patient panel with quick facts: blood group, active admission status, recent appointment, department context - Create bed request/admission request workflow with searchable patient picker, diagnosis, care level, and notes - Bed request history with status, assigned bed, timeline, and next steps  5. Nurse experience - Nurse dashboard with department census, admitted count, with-bed vs without-bed count, monitored last 24 hours - Patient monitoring list with search and status filters - Admission detail or bedside monitoring workspace with patient identity, blood group, diagnosis, bed assignment, recent medical records, and recent vitals - Vital signs entry form for temperature, pulse, blood pressure, respiration, SpO2, and notes - Recent vitals table and medical record timeline - Special Blood Bank nurse mode for donor screening, donor detail, health check entry, eligibility result, and donor health history  6. Patient experience - Patient portal overview with profile, blood group, emergency contacts, upcoming appointments, medical record count, and active blood requests - Appointment booking flow with department selection, optional doctor selection, calendar/date-time picker, and confirmation state - Appointment management table with status, doctor, department, date, and cancel action - Medical records page with searchable table, detail drawer, treatment plan, clinician, and admission reference - Blood request form with blood group, units, component, urgency, department/admission context, and notes - Blood request tracking page with status timeline, accepted donors, and fulfillment updates - Patient profile/settings page with editable personal and emergency contact details  7. Blood Bank and donor operations - Blood Matching Center for admin or blood bank staff with urgency-first request board - Request board with filters for status, department, blood group, and blood bank - Selected request panel with patient context, units needed, component, available inventory, accepted donors, and next-step actions - Compatible donor suggestion cards with match score, compatibility label, eligibility, last donation date, availability, and latest health check - Match timeline showing notification sent, donor read, donor response, acceptance, approval, and fulfillment - Staff donor directory and donor search - Donation logging flow linked to donor screening and optional linked blood request - Blood bank administration screens for blood banks, donor profiles, inventory rows, and request overview - Inventory views by bank, blood group, component, and units available  8. Donor experience - Donor dashboard with eligibility badge, availability, request notifications, donation history, and lifetime stats - Weekly availability form and history table - Notification center with clear Accept / Decline actions - Donation history list with bank, date, component, units, and linked request status - Donor profile summary and readiness state  9. Applicant experience - Applicant workspace with latest application status, waiting state, review note, application history, and next-step guidance - Clear messaging for pending review, approved next actions, or rejection feedback  For all dashboards and data screens: - Use clean KPI cards, card-and-table hybrid layouts, sticky filter toolbars, row actions, contextual drawers, and modals - Show meaningful hierarchy and triage: urgent blood requests, abnormal vitals, admissions without beds, appointments today, frozen accounts - Prioritize clarity over decoration; every page should make the next action obvious  State design is mandatory: - Loading state for every page, table, card list, form submit, and detail drawer - Empty state for no applications, no appointments, no medical records, no donors, no admissions, no beds, no notifications, and no inventory - Error state with friendly human-readable messages and retry actions - Permission and access-denied state - Incomplete setup state for staff whose profile or department assignment is not configured yet - Success toasts, inline banners, and destructive confirmation dialogs  Accessibility requirements: - WCAG AA contrast - Clear keyboard focus states - Large click/tap targets for tablet use - Never rely on color alone for status - Use icon + label + text for important states - Make dense medical data readable with strong alignment and spacing - Surface patient identity, blood group, department, and urgency clearly for safety  Responsive requirements: - Design for desktop first, with tablet adaptations - Create desktop and tablet frames for the main app shell and major role dashboards - Sidebar can collapse on tablet, but hierarchy and primary actions must remain obvious  Use realistic sample healthcare data and role-specific content throughout. Make the result feel like a polished production healthcare product, not a prototype. Generate a cohesive Figma-ready UI system with reusable components, variants, and full high-fidelity screens.","providerOptions":{}}

- React Router setup

- Professional healthcare aesthetics
